provenance.quote: At an ongoing estimated annual expense of $760,000 to $1,300,000 from County revenue that supports public safety, transportation, and essential county services, shall the membership of the Douglas County Board of Commissioners be increased from a three-member board to a five-member board?

If the membership of the Douglas County Board of Commissioners is increased from a three- member board to a five-member board, by what method shall the Douglas County Board of Commissioners be elected? (Vote for One) Five District Commissioners who reside in districts to be elected by the voters only by the voters resident in the district; or Three District Commissioners who reside in districts to be elected by the voters only by the voters resident in the district, and two At-Large Commissioners to be elected by the voters of the whole county.
In the event the Douglas County Board of Commissioners is increased to five members, shall all registered Douglas County voters continue to elect all County Commissioners?

contests.title: City of Castle Pines Ballot Question 300

provenance.quote: Should the City of Castle Pines Home Rule Charter be amended to include the following provision: Property in excess of 20 acres owned or controlled by a single owner or ownership group or that are part of a common plan of development or related transactions may be annexed into the City only upon approval by the voters at an election of the registered electors of the City of Castle Pines, Colorado, and for purposes of this provision, any single, successive, cumulative, serial or simultaneous annexations of multiple parcels shall be aggregated and treated as a single annexation as provided in C.R.S. Section 31-12-104(1)(a)?

contests.title: City of Castle Pines Ballot Question 301

provenance.quote: Should the City of Castle Pines Home Rule Charter be amended to include the following provision: Any parcel over 20 acres owned or controlled by a single owner or ownership group annexed within 180 days of the effective date of this section shall be referred for ratification at an election of the registered electors of the City of Castle Pines, Colorado, and if no such annexation occurs within such 180-day period, this section may be repealed by Council ordinance without a vote of the registered electors of the City of Castle Pines, Colorado?

SHALL CITY OF AURORA TAXES BE INCREASED UP TO $12,640,000 AND AS MAY BE GENERATED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER BY THE IMPOSITION OF A NEW 0.129% SALES AND USE TAX (THAT EQUALS 12.9 CENTS ON EVERY ONE HUNDRED DOLLAR PURCHASE) FOR A PERIOD BEGINNING ON JANUARY 1, 2027, AND ENDING ON DECEMBER 31, 2057, TO PROVIDE FOR THE OPERATION OF AND REPAIRS, MAINTENANCE, AND IMPROVEMENTS TO COMMUNITY FACILITIES, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION LIBRARIES, RECREATION AND COMMUNITY CENTERS; AND SHALL CITY OF AURORA DEBT BE INCREASED BY AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $105,000,000 WITH A MAXIMUM REPAYMENT COST OF UP TO $204,870,000 TO ACCOMPLISH THE PURPOSES STATED ABOVE, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: PARK RENOVATIONS AND NEW PARK CONSTRUCTION; RECREATION CENTER IMPROVEMENTS AND NEW RECREATION CENTER CONSTRUCTION; LIBRARY BRANCH IMPROVEMENTS AND NEW LIBRARY CONSTRUCTION; SUCH DEBT TO CONSIST OF REVENUE BONDS WHICH SHALL BEAR INTEREST, MATURE, BE SUBJECT TO REDEMPTION, WITH OR WITHOUT PREMIUM, AND BE ISSUED, DATED AND SOLD (AT, ABOVE OR BELOW PAR) IN SUCH MANNER AND CONTAINING SUCH OTHER TERMS, NOT INCONSISTENT HEREWITH, AS THE CITY COUNCIL MAY DETERMINE; SHALL THE CITY OF AURORA BE AUTHORIZED TO PAY SUCH BONDS FROM, AND TO SECURE SUCH PAYMENT BY A PLEDGE OF, THE NEW 0.129% SALES AND USE TAX AND OTHER LEGALLY AVAILABLE FUNDS; AND SHALL THE CITY OF AURORA BE ENTITLED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND SPEND THE FULL REVENUES FROM SUCH TAX INCREASE AND THE PROCEEDS OF ANY INVESTMENT THEREOF NOTWITHSTANDING ANY LIMITATION IN THE STATE CONSTITUTION, STATE LAW OR THE CITY HOME RULE CHARTER?

contests.title: Douglas County School District RE-1 — General Fund Tax Question

provenance.quote: SHALL DOUGLAS COUNTY SCHOOL DISTRICT RE-1 TAXES BE INCREASED $54 MILLION COMMENCING IN 2026 FOR TAX COLLECTION IN YEAR 2027 TO BE USED FOR GENERAL FUND PURPOSES INCLUDING: RETAIN AND ATTRACT TOP QUALITY TEACHERS AND STAFF, WITH SALARIES TO BE MORE COMPETITIVE WITH NEIGHBORING DISTRICTS, AND TO BETTER KEEP PACE WITH INFLATION; SUPPORT INCREASING COSTS OF SCHOOL SECURITY, INCLUDING SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICERS; REDUCE STUDENT WAITLISTS FOR CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION PROGRAMMING, INCLUDING THE TRADES; RESTORE STUDENT PROGRAMMING, SUCH AS INSTRUMENTAL MUSIC IN ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS; AND BE IMPOSED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER FOR THE ABOVE PURPOSES BY WHATEVER AMOUNTS ARE RAISED BY THE IMPOSITION OF A MILL LEVY WHICH, WHEN COMBINED WITH PRIOR VOTER APPROVED OVERRIDE QUESTIONS, SHALL PRODUCE REVENUE NOT TO EXCEED THE LIMIT ESTABLISHED FOR THE DISTRICT BY SECTION 22-54-108(3)(B) (VI), C.R.S., AND SHALL THE REVENUES FROM SUCH TAXES AND ANY EARNINGS FROM THE INVESTMENT OF SUCH REVENUES BE COLLECTED AND SPENT AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION AND ANY OTHER LAW; AND SHALL THE DISTRICT'S EXPENDITURES BE SUBJECT TO AN ANNUAL INDEPENDENT AUDIT POSTED ON ITS WEBSITE AND BE SUBJECT TO OVERSIGHT BY A CITIZENS' COMMITTEE?

contests.title: Larkspur Fire Protection District Ballot Issue 6A

provenance.quote: SHALL LARKSPUR FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT (LFPD) TAXES BE INCREASED $925,225 ANNUALLY (IN THE FIRST FULL FISCAL YEAR), AND BY SUCH AMOUNT AS ARE RAISED THEREAFTER, BEGINNING JANUARY 1, 2027, BY INCREASING THE DISTRICT'S PROPERTY TAX RATE BY 3.97 MILLS FOR THE PURPOSES OF MAINTAINING AND ENHANCING THE CURRENT OPERATIONS IN FIRE PROTECTION, EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONSE, PUBLIC SAFETY, AND RELATED SERVICES FOR THE RESIDENTS, PROPERTY OWNERS, VISITORS, AND BUSINESSES SERVED BY THE DISTRICT, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: • INCREASE FIREFIGHTER STAFFING TO DECREASE RESPONSE TIMES, INCREASE COVERAGE; • PROVIDE HIGH-QUALITY TRAINING THAT ENSURE OUR FIREFIGHTERS ARE PREPARED FOR ANY FORESEEABLE EMERGENCY; • PROVIDE COMPETITIVE WAGES AND BENEFITS COMPARED TO SIMILAR FIRE AGENCIES FOR RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF HIGHLY QUALIFIED FIREFIGHTERS AND OTHER PERSONNEL; • PARTICIPATE IN AN ACCREDITATION PROCESS TO HELP WITH STABILIZING THE INSURANCE OF PROPERTIES IN THE DISTRICT AND VALIDATING THE SERVICES PROVIDED TO THE COMMUNITY; • SUSTAIN FUNDING TO MAINTAIN OUR FLEET OF EMERGENCY VEHICLES, FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT SO THEY ARE OPTIMIZED TO BE INLINE WITH THE STRATEGIC PLANS AND OPERATIONAL NEEDS; AND IN ORDER TO FACILITATE CONTINUED FINANCIAL STABILITY, SHALL THE DISTRICT BE AUTHORIZED TO OFFSET THE POSSIBILITIES OF REVENUE LOSS DUE TO LEGISLATIVE CHANGES, REDUCED REVENUE DUE TO DECREASED PROPERTY VALUATION, OR OTHER MATTERS THAT WOULD REDUCE THE DISTRICT’S TOTAL REVENUE FROM CURRENT LEVELS AND ACCOUNTING FOR GROWTH WITHIN THE DISTRICT, BY PERIODICALLY ADJUSTING THE MILL LEVY RATE, AS NEEDED TO REMAIN REVENUE NEUTRAL, STARTING TAX COLLECTION YEAR 2028 AND REVIEWED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER AND SHALL ALL DISTRICT REVENUES BE COLLECTED, RETAINED, AND SPEND NOTWITHSTANDING ANY REVENUE LIMITS PROVIDED BY LAW?

contests.title: Larkspur Fire Protection District Ballot Issue 6B

provenance.quote: SHALL LARKSPUR FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT (LFPD) DEBT BE INCREASED $4.5 MILLION, WITH A REPAYMENT COST OF UP TO $6.4 MILLION, AND SHALL DISTRICT TAXES BE INCREASED UP TO $427,333 ANNUALLY TO PAY SUCH DEBT, SUCH DEBT TO BE USED FOR CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS OF THE DISTRICT, INCLUDING: • PURCHASE OF FIRE/EMS EQUIPMENT AND/OR APPARATUS TO REPLACE AGING AND OUTDATED RESPONSE VEHICLES; • DESIGN, ACQUISITION, AND INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS FOR FUTURE STATION IN THE SOUTHEASTERN AREA OF THE DISTRICT RESPONSE JURISDICTION; • DESIGN, INSTALLATION, AND CONSTRUCTION OF TRAINING GROUNDS INFRASTRUCTURE; • PURCHASE OF TRAINING GROUNDS SIMULATORS AND EQUIPMENT TO TRAIN FIREFIGHTERS IN MULTIPLE CERTIFICATION LEVELS; • ACQUIRING CAPITAL ASSETS BY EXERCISING THE DISTRICT'S BEST OPTIONS TO PREPAY EXISTING LEASE OBLIGATIONS SUCH DEBT TO BE EVIDENCED BY THE ISSUANCE OF GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS OR ANY OTHER MULTIPLE YEAR FINANCIAL OBLIGATION OF THE DISTRICT; SUCH BONDS TO BE SOLD IN ONE SERIES OR MORE, FOR A PRICE ABOVE OR BELOW THE PRINCIPAL AMOUNT OF SUCH SERIES, ON TERMS AND CONDITIONS, AND WITH SUCH MATURITIES AS PERMITTED BY LAW AND AS THE DISTRICT MAY DETERMINE, INCLUDING PROVISIONS FOR REDEMPTION OF THE BONDS PRIOR TO MATURITY WITH OR WITHOUT PAYMENT OF THE PREMIUM OF NOT TO EXCEED THREE PERCENT; AND SHALL SUCH TAX REVENUES AND THE EARNINGS FROM THE INVESTMENT OF SUCH BOND PROCEEDS AND TAX REVENUES BE COLLECTED, RETAINED AND SPENT AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION OR ANY OTHER LAW?

contests.title: Stone Creek Metropolitan District Ballot Question 6C

provenance.quote: Shall all unused debt authorization granted by the voters in all prior elections to Stone Creek Metropolitan District be forever repealed and rescinded effective immediately?

contests.title: Stone Creek Metropolitan District Ballot Question 6D

provenance.quote: Shall Ballot Issue 5C, unanimously approved by three voters at a special election held on November 4, 2014, be forever repealed and rescinded effective immediately, which ballot issue authorizes Stone Creek Metropolitan District to enter into one or more multiple fiscal year financial obligations evidenced by intergovernmental agreements or contracts and to increase ad valorem taxes up to $1 million annually to fund such agreements?

contests.title: Stone Creek Metropolitan District Ballot Question 6E

provenance.quote: Shall Ballot Issue 5D, unanimously approved by three voters at a special election held on November 4, 2014, be forever repealed and rescinded effective immediately, which ballot issue authorizes Stone Creek Metropolitan District to enter into one or more multiple fiscal year financial obligations evidenced by intergovernmental agreements or contracts to fund regional improvements and to increase ad valorem taxes up to $1 million per year to fund such agreements?

contests.title: Stone Creek Metropolitan District Ballot Question 6F

provenance.quote: Shall Ballot Issue 5S, unanimously approved by three voters at a special election held on November 4, 2014, be forever repealed and rescinded effective immediately, which ballot issue authorizes Stone Creek Metropolitan District to enter into one or more intergovernmental agreements, which agreement may constitute a multiple fiscal year financial obligation of the District, for the purpose of jointly financing the costs of any public improvements, facilities, systems, programs, or projects which the District may lawfully provide, or for the purpose of providing for the operations and maintenance of the District and its facilities and properties?

contests.title: Stone Creek Metropolitan District Ballot Question 6G

provenance.quote: Shall Ballot Issue 5T, unanimously approved by three voters at a special election held on November 4, 2014, be forever repealed and rescinded effective immediately, which ballot issue authorizes Stone Creek Metropolitan District to enter into one or more multiple fiscal year financial obligations evidenced by intergovernmental agreements concerning the provision of public improvements with a regional authority or one or more other political subdivisions or governmentally-owned enterprises, containing such terms and conditions as the District Board of Directors may determine to be necessary and appropriate and providing for payments by the District in an aggregate amount not to exceed $82,800,000 of tax revenues derived from an ad valorem mill levy imposed by the District on all taxable property?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase the Douglas County Board of Commissioners from three members to five. The ballot estimates an ongoing annual cost of $760,000 to $1.3 million, paid from county revenue that also supports public safety, transportation and other essential county services.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve expanding the county board to five members.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the board at three members.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Choose an election method if Douglas County’s commission expands to five members. One option elects all five commissioners by district, with each commissioner living in the district and elected only by its voters. The other elects three district-resident commissioners only by voters in those districts, and two commissioners countywide. This is a choice between two methods, rather than a yes-or-no question. It applies only if the board expands.
If Douglas County’s board grows to five commissioners, continue having all registered county voters elect every commissioner, rather than limiting some or all seats to voters of individual districts.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve countywide voting for every commissioner if the board expands.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this requirement for countywide voting if the board expands.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Require a Castle Pines voter election before annexing more than 20 acres owned or controlled by one owner or ownership group, or connected through a common development plan or related transactions. Related parcels annexed in single, successive, cumulative or simultaneous transactions would be combined when applying the rule.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Add the voter-approval requirement for these annexations to the city charter.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not add this annexation requirement to the charter.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Require a ratification election for annexation of a parcel over 20 acres owned or controlled by one owner or ownership group when annexed within 180 days of this charter section’s effective date. If no such annexation occurs in that 180-day period, the council could repeal the section by ordinance without a voter election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the annexation-ratification rule and the council’s conditional repeal authority.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not add this rule to the city charter.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.129% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $12.64 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of libraries, recreation and community centers, and construction and renovation of parks, recreation centers and library branches. Authorize up to $105 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $204.87 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.064% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $6.27 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of police, fire and other public-safety infrastructure and facilities, including fire stations, Aurora 911 and police facilities. Authorize up to $53 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $101.6 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Create a dedicated 0.132% Aurora sales and use tax from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2057. It would raise up to $12.94 million initially and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Revenue would support operation, repair and improvement of transportation infrastructure and facilities, including traffic, intersection and pedestrian safety, bridge replacements, and roadway improvements and expansion. Authorize up to $108 million in revenue bonds, with total repayment capped at $209.733 million, paid from the new tax and other legally available funds. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be kept and spent despite limits in the Colorado Constitution, state law and the city charter.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the dedicated sales and use tax, borrowing and revenue-limit exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this tax, borrowing or the related revenue-limit exceptions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Move Aurora’s regular municipal elections from odd-numbered years to even-numbered years. Change the charter to allow one-time shorter terms of office needed for the transition.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve moving municipal elections to even-numbered years and the transition terms.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing election schedule and do not approve these transition changes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Douglas County School District RE-1 property taxes by $54 million in 2026 for collection in 2027. Money would support general-fund purposes, including staff compensation, school security, career and technical education and restoring student programs such as elementary instrumental music. In later years, a property-tax levy combined with earlier voter-approved overrides could raise up to the district’s statutory limit. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits. Spending would receive an annual independent audit posted online and oversight by a citizens’ committee.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional education taxes, audit and citizen oversight, and revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add 3.97 mills to Larkspur Fire Protection District’s property-tax rate beginning January 1, 2027, raising $925,225 in the first full fiscal year and amounts based on collections later. Money would support fire and medical response, staffing, training, pay and benefits, accreditation, vehicles, facilities and equipment. Starting in tax collection year 2028, the district could adjust the levy to offset revenue losses from legislative changes, lower property values or other causes while accounting for growth, with annual review. District revenue could be collected, kept and spent despite legal revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the property-tax increase, later levy adjustments to maintain revenue and the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this increase, adjustment authority or proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize $4.5 million in Larkspur Fire Protection District debt, with total repayment capped at $6.4 million, and up to $427,333 in additional taxes annually to repay it. Projects include fire and emergency-medical vehicles and equipment, design and infrastructure for a future southeastern station, training grounds and simulators, and acquiring capital assets by prepaying existing leases. Debt could be general-obligation bonds or other multiyear obligations. Early repayment could include a premium of up to 3%. Tax revenue and investment earnings on taxes and bonds could be spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the capital debt, taxes to repay it and the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this borrowing, additional taxes or related revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently cancel all permission for Stone Creek Metropolitan District to borrow that voters approved in earlier elections but the district has not used.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal the district’s unused debt authorizations.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5C. That measure authorizes multiyear financial obligations through intergovernmental agreements or contracts and property taxes of up to $1 million annually to fund them.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authority for these multiyear obligations and related taxes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5D. That measure authorizes multiyear financial obligations through agreements or contracts for regional improvements and property taxes of up to $1 million annually to fund them.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authority for these regional-improvement obligations and related taxes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5S. That measure allows intergovernmental agreements, which may create multiyear financial obligations, to jointly finance lawful public improvements and programs or district operations and maintenance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal this 2014 authority for intergovernmental financing agreements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal Stone Creek’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5T. That measure authorizes multiyear intergovernmental obligations for public improvements with regional authorities, other governments or government-owned enterprises. It permits up to $82.8 million in total district payments from property-tax revenue.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Repeal this 2014 authority for intergovernmental obligations and property-tax-funded payments.
